newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold seen ranging, platinum eyes $400.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold seen ranging, platinum eyes $400.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Gold prices are likely to range between $340.00 and $345.00 an ounce in the near term, but several traders and chartists suggest prices will eventually turn lower against a backdrop of charts in a downtrend.
Platinum is thin on the ground and eyeing $400, while sister metal palladium is targeting $185 after breaking above $180.
GOLD - Gold was expected to remain locked in a $340-$345 range on Wednesday, but was still adopting a downside bias after a recent corrective bounce.
Chart resistance was likely to be found from the 10- and 30-day moving averages at $345.19 and $343.20. Several chartists suggested gold might move and test important support at $339.50.
At 0816 spot gold was indicated at $342.60/3.10, versus Tuesday's London close of $342.50/$343.00.
PLATINUM - Eyeing levels towards $400 as shorts continued to cover a market devoid of large amounts of material.

News that Russian deliveries of platinum group metals in 1997 were seen about the same as in 1996 was largely ignored. Traders said supplies would remain tight over the coming months even with the resumption of Russian shipments .
At 0816 GMT platinum was indicated at $397.00/$398.00, against $393.50/$394.50.
PALLADIUM - Seen moving on $185 after breaching $180.00. Volatile trading expected.
At 0816 GMT it was quoted at $180.00/$181.00, compared with $177.75/$178.75.
SILVER - Seen quiet between $4.60 and $4.80. Last quoted at $4.68/70, down two cents.
